scenes.name: Born of Fire
scenes.display: In the kingdom of Pañchāla, King Drupada kindled a great sacrificial fire — and out of the flames arose a daughter. Draupadī: dark, radiant, born of no womb. The gods whispered that she would bend the fate of kings.
scenes.tts: In the kingdom of Pun-chaala, King Droo-pada kindled a great sacrificial fire; and out of the flames arose a daughter. Drow-pa-dee. Dark, radiant, born of no womb. The gods whispered, that she would bend the fate of kings.

scenes.name: The Svayaṃvara
scenes.display: When she came of age, kings from every land filled Drupada's hall. High above hung a golden fish, spinning on a wheel. Whoever could string the great bow, and pierce the fish's eye by its reflection alone, would win her hand.
scenes.tts: When she came of age, kings from every land filled Droo-pada's hall. High above hung a golden fish, spinning on a wheel. Whoever could string the great bow, and pierce the fish's eye by its reflection alone, would win her hand.

scenes.name: The Kings Fail
scenes.display: One by one, the proud kings strained against the bow — and one by one they fell back, defeated. Even Karṇa the golden rose to try; but Draupadī turned her face away.
scenes.tts: One by one, the proud kings strained against the bow; and one by one they fell back, defeated. Even Kurna the golden rose to try; but Drow-pa-dee turned her face away.

scenes.name: A Stranger in White
scenes.display: Then, from among the brahmins, a quiet young man in white stood up. The five Pāṇḍava brothers, believed dead in the burning of the lac house, had come to Pañchāla in disguise. His name was Arjuna.
scenes.tts: Then, from among the brah-mins, a quiet young man in white stood up. The five Paan-dava brothers, believed dead in the burning of the lack house, had come to Pun-chaala in disguise. His name was Ar-joona.

scenes.name: The Eye of the Fish
scenes.display: He circled the bow, and bowed his head. In a single breath he strung it. Then, gazing only into the water — at the trembling reflection of the wheel — he loosed five arrows into the sky.
scenes.tts: He circled the bow, and bowed his head. In a single breath, he strung it. Then, gazing only into the water, at the trembling reflection of the wheel, he loosed five arrows into the sky.

scenes.name: The Garland
scenes.display: The golden fish fell. And Draupadī came to the stranger, and laid her garland of white flowers upon his neck. In the crowd, Kṛṣṇa smiled — for he alone had recognized the brahmin.
scenes.tts: The golden fish fell. And Drow-pa-dee came to the stranger, and laid her garland of white flowers upon his neck. In the crowd, Krish-na smiled; for he alone had recognized the brah-min.

scenes.name: A Mother's Word
scenes.display: That evening, at their mother's door, the brothers called out: "Mother — see what we have brought!" And Kuntī, without turning, answered: "Share it among yourselves." A mother's word, once spoken, could not be unsaid.
scenes.tts: That evening, at their mother's door, the brothers called out: Mother! See what we have brought! And Koon-tee, without turning, answered: share it among yourselves. A mother's word, once spoken, could not be unsaid.

scenes.name: Five Flames, One Fate
scenes.display: But the sage Vyāsa revealed a deeper design: in a former life, Draupadī had prayed five times to Lord Śiva for a worthy husband — and Śiva had granted all five prayers. And so Draupadī wed the five Pāṇḍava brothers; and their fates were bound together, until the end of the age.
scenes.tts: But the sage Vee-yaasa revealed a deeper design. In a former life, Drow-pa-dee had prayed five times to Lord Shiva, for a worthy husband; and Shiva had granted all five prayers. And so Drow-pa-dee wed the five Paan-dava brothers; and their fates were bound together, until the end of the age.
